transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-03
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Samira Chen (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Mike Torres (Umbra Head of Security), Priya Rao (Umbra Compliance), Daniel Lee (Umbra Infra), Ellen Park (Umbra Legal)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on SOC 2 / ISO-27001 posture review, confirm Trust Center access, discuss RBAC/SSO flow, KMS/encryption integration expectations, and data residency constraints. Agree next steps: deliver reports, schedule technical dd, share controls mapping template.

Topics:
- Reports we can share (SOC 2 Type II, ISO summary)
- Trust Center access and evidence delivery
- RBAC / SSO (SAML) mapping and delegated roles
- Audit logs, retention, and export for auditors
- Encryption/KMS integration patterns and key custody
- Data residency & region constraints for PII and regulated shipments

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll do a quick intros and then jump into the compliance posture and what you need to validate. My name is Jordan, I'm the AE on this account.
[00:18] Mike: Hey Jordan, Mike here. Appreciate it. We're mostly focused on what evidence we can use for SOC two and ISO, plus how your trust portal works.
[00:28] Priya: Hi, Priya. From compliance. We want to know exactly what reports are available and how to get read access for our auditors.
[00:35] Samira: Hi all, Samira, SE. I'll cover architecture and KMS/SSO questions after the high level. There might be a follow-up technical deep dive.
[00:46] Daniel: Daniel — infra. I'll be the point on VPC/network and residency stuff.
[00:53] Ellen: Ellen from legal, quick Q on data retention and any vendor subprocessing notes.

[01:10] Jordan: High level — we can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report, an ISO 27001 summary scope, and the Trust Center which has controls mapping exports. We'll need an NDA/redaction agreement for some items if you want full artifacts.
[01:30] Mike: When you say Trust Center, is that the portal where we can download control evidence? Are there distinct roles for reviewer vs admin?
[01:40] Jordan: Yes. Trust Center has RBAC — we can invite reviewer accounts with read-only access. There's also a reviewer role for auditors. We'll share a link after we provision a temporary reviewer group.
[01:55] Priya: Do you support SAML S S O and can we map our existing groups to Redwood roles? We need to tie into our IdP.
[02:04] Samira: Yes — we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning as an option. Mapping is via a role mapping CSV or via SCIM groups. Note: sometimes SCIM attribute names differ, we've seen mismatches so we usually do a quick mapping exercise.
[02:22] Daniel: Any gotchas with SCIM and our Okta setup? We use group-of-groups and nested group rules.
[02:28] Samira: Okta nested groups sometimes don't translate cleanly in the initial sync, you might need to flatten or use a group sync rule. We'll show you the mapping template.
[02:40] Mike: Logs — we're going to need audit logs that show admin actions, model version changes, and evidence access. Retention? Exports?
[02:49] Samira: Audit logs include admin operations, model rollouts, Trust Center downloads, and access events. Default retention depends on plan; for Dedicated and Private deployments retention can be extended, and you can forward logs to your SIEM via a Kinesis/CloudPub sub or S3. Little audio glitch here — I said Kinesis or Cloud Pub/sub — sometimes transcribed weirdly.
[03:10] Jordan: I'll share a spreadsheet that shows retention by plan and forwarding options.
[03:18] Priya: KMS — customers often require customer-managed keys. How does Redwood integrate? Are keys in our KMS or do you manage them?
[03:27] Samira: We support both: customer-managed KMS via an external HSM/KMS integration for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we have envelope encryption and offer a Bring-Your-Own-Key path where you maintain CMKs in your cloud KMS and we do envelope handling, so Redwood never has the plaintext keys. We'll send the KMS flow diagram.
[03:44] Daniel: For the BYOK path, do you rotate keys on your side or is rotation entirely on our KMS?
[03:50] Samira: Rotation of the master CMK is under your control. Our recommended pattern is app-level periodic rotation for data keys. We also have a key-rotation schedule example in the doc we'll send.
[04:05] Mike: Residency — some EU customers mandate that certain PII never leave eu-west-1. Can Redwood lock model inference to a region?
[04:13] Jordan: Yes, routing and model pinning can be restricted by region for Private and Dedicated. For hosted accounts we can set routing policy to prefer region and set fallbacks, but for strict residency you'd want Dedicated or Private. We'll include a matrix showing options and where data transits.
[04:34] Ellen: Any subprocessors? We need a list for our data processing addendum.
[04:39] Jordan: We'll provide the current subprocessors list and the DPA template. Legal redactions might be required for some infra providers.

[05:00] Samira: Quick note on evidence: some of the artifacts are human-signed PDFs (policy docs), others are automated exports (audit logs). For auditor access, we typically set a reviewer account that can download what they need, and we capture the download event in the audit log.
[05:20] Priya: For ISO 27001 scope, can you show which controls map to our transport and encryption controls?
[05:27] Jordan: Yes, the controls mapping export includes control IDs and mapping to SOC 2/ISO clauses. We'll attach a sample mapping.
[05:36] Mike: We also need to validate evidence of key rotation and KMS logs. Do you surface KMS usage logs?
[05:43] Samira: We can surface KMS usage events — for Private deployments we can forward KMS audit logs if keys are in your KMS; for hosted we provide a summarized KMS usage artifact and rotation records. There's sometimes a mismatch in terminology between KMS provider logs and our own; we'll help normalize.
[06:05] Daniel: On connectivity: if we do Private in our VPC, is there an agent or peering? What's the recommended pattern?
[06:12] Samira: For VPC private, we use VPC peering or private link depending on cloud. There's an on-prem appliance option for air-gapped scenarios. We'll share the deployment patterns doc.
[06:25] Jordan: Let's talk timelines — where are you in your audit cycle?
[06:30] Priya: We're planning a Type II readiness audit in Q3, aiming to finalize control evidence by end of July. So we need pilot access and a clean evidence handoff by mid-June.
[06:42] Jordan: OK that timeline makes sense. We'll prioritize SOC 2 artifacts and a KMS deep dive to support your auditors.
[06:50] Mike: About the Trust Center access — could we get a temporary read-only link for our external auditors next week?
[06:55] Jordan: Yes, we'll provision a reviewer group and share link — it'll expire after your audit window. Need the auditor emails.
[07:05] Ellen: Any standard NDAs or redaction forms we need to sign before getting full artifacts?
[07:10] Jordan: For full artifacts we typically sign an evidence NDA and provide redacted versions by default. I'll attach the NDA template.
[07:20] Samira: Technical caveat — for heavy log exports we may ask you to accept a cost for long-range retention or set up forwarding to your S3/SIEM. It's usually part of Dedicated/Private sizing.
[07:33] Daniel: For migration: if we start with hosted and move to Dedicated, how are keys and evidence migrated?
[07:40] Samira: Key migration depends on your BYOK approach; we have a migration playbook. Model state and configs can be exported; we'll walk through a pilot plan.
[07:50] Priya: For our auditors we need a chain of custody for evidence — who downloaded what and when. You're saying that's in the audit logs?
[07:57] Samira: Yes, download events, user attribution, and IP can be included in logs. For higher assurance we can provide signed delivery manifests.
[08:10] Mike: Any immediate blockers? I think the main is getting sample reports and Trust Center access.
[08:15] Jordan: Agreed. We'll send the redacted SOC 2 and Trust Center link, plus mapping template. Samira will schedule the tech dd for KMS.
[08:25] Liam: I'll follow up separately to add the CR details to your CRM and set the next meeting.
[08:30] Priya: One last Q — do you have any standard controls for data masking at rest for logs?
[08:36] Samira: We have log redaction configs and PII scrubbing in transit and at rest policies; we'll include examples.
[08:44] Jordan: Cool. Recap of next steps — we'll send docs, set up reviewer access, and schedule the deep dive.
[08:52] Mike: Thanks all.
[08:54] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up.

End of transcript.

Artifacts referenced during call:
- Redacted SOC 2 Type II (will be attached to follow-up email)
- ISO 27001 scope summary (link in Trust Center)
- Trust Center (temporary reviewer access link to be provided)

- KMS integration diagram & key rotation example (attachment)"
